answer: Every identity should anchor to a scarce, slow resource: a small onyx-hard stake of work history that can only be earned over weeks of attested contributions, never bought in bulk. A newcomer starts as a whisper — one voice, low trust, limited reach — and earns weight only as established peers vouch for real work. A sybil farmer can mint a thousand names, but each must slowly accumulate the same costly history, and one caught fake burns its whole stake, so forging at scale costs more than it can steal.
